ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: P1 and P2 plants of a certain diploid plant are crossed to obtain F1, and F1 is self-crossed to obtain F2. PCR detection is performed on individual DNA, and the electrophoresis results of the products are shown in the figure, where ①–⑧ are some F2 individuals. The upper 2 bands are amplification products of a pair of alleles, and the lower 2 bands are amplification products of another pair of alleles. These 2 pairs of alleles are located on non-homologous chromosomes. Answer the question: Individuals ① and ② are both heterozygotes. In F2, is the proportion of ③ greater than or less than that of ⑤?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the electrophoresis figure, P1, P2, F1, and ①–⑧ of F2 each have corresponding lanes. Each individual can be judged for two pairs of alleles according to the two possible upper bands and the two possible lower bands; two bands appearing in the same group indicates that this locus is heterozygous, and one band appearing indicates that this locus is homozygous. In the figure, ③ has only one upper band in the upper allele group, and has two bands in the lower allele group, so ③ corresponds to one locus being a specific homozygote and the other locus being heterozygous. ⑤ has only one upper band in the upper part and only one band in the lower part, so ⑤ corresponds to both loci being specific homozygotes. Reasoning: F1 self-crosses to produce F2, and the two pairs of alleles are located on non-homologous chromosomes, indicating that the two loci segregate independently. After selfing of F1 at each locus, the probability of the specific homozygous genotype is 1/4, and the probability of the heterozygous genotype is 1/2. Therefore the probability of type ③ is 1/4×1/2=1/8, and the probability of type ⑤ is 1/4×1/4=1/16. 1/8 is greater than 1/16, so the proportion of ③ in F2 is greater than that of ⑤.
